drafted_from: tool:read-a-page-of-messages-on-this-mac's own row and tools/notice-when-something-shows-up/tests/read-a-page-of-messages.test.mjs (a real SQLite file with the Messages tables, made-up numbers); read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the 40 newest messages on this Mac that my history does not hold yet, without telling anyone". It runs tool:read-a-page-of-messages-on-this-mac once with max_facts 40 and gives back each message as the same fact the watcher tells for a new one, with next_before_row to start the next page from.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it only reads Messages and answers facts, and the workflow that calls it keeps the statements.
instructions: 1. Give the app that runs your engine on this Mac Full Disk Access: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access. macOS lets no program read Messages without it.

2. Grant tool:read-a-page-of-messages-on-this-mac the read-messages capability at your engine's grants door, as tool:notice-messages-on-this-mac holds it; a run without the grant is refused before it starts.

3. Run it with the Messages database as an absolute path (inside a Mac sandbox the home folder is not yours): input {database: "<your home folder>/Library/Messages/chat.db", max_facts: 40}. Left out, before_row starts from the newest message.

4. Read what comes back: facts (newest first; each has where, place message, change added, at, key, by, after, kinds), next_before_row and done. Give next_before_row as before_row for the next page; done true means no message is left below it.
5. It only reads and tells the engine nothing. To keep the facts in your history, use workflow:backfill-a-message-source-from-a-position, which calls it page by page and keeps each fact once.
